text: The first applicant is a legal entity registered under Georgian law on 8 November 2010.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: With the exception of the first applicant, the remaining fourteen applicants live in Tbilisi.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The dates of birth of the applicants are indicated in the attached annex to the judgment.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The first applicant is a Georgian non-governmental organisation set up to promote and protect the rights of lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender (LGBT) people in Georgia.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The first applicant planned to organise a peaceful march on 17 May 2012 in the centre of Tbilisi.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The peaceful march planned by the first applicant was intended to mark the International Day Against Homophobia.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 8 May 2012, the first applicant gave the Tbilisi City Hall prior notice of its intention to hold a peaceful demonstration on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 8 May 2012, the first applicant gave the Ministry of the Interior prior notice of its intention to hold a peaceful demonstration on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The first applicant informed the authorities of the planned route of the march, which would start from the grounds of the Tbilisi Concert Hall and proceed to Orbeliani Square.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The first applicant informed the authorities of the approximate number of participants in the planned march.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In light of a foreseeable protest from those opposed to the LGBT community in Georgia and the general background of hostility towards sexual minorities, the first applicant specifically requested that the authorities provide sufficient protection from possible violence.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 14 May 2012, the Tbilisi City Hall acknowledged receipt of the first applicant's request of 8 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 14 May 2012, the Tbilisi City Hall explained to the first applicant the rights and responsibilities of demonstrators as provided for by the relevant law.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 15 May 2012, the first applicant organisation was contacted by a senior officer of the Ministry of the Interior.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The senior officer of the Ministry of the Interior clarified the details of the planned march of 17 May 2012 with the first applicant organisation.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The senior officer of the Ministry of the Interior confirmed to the first applicant organisation that police forces would be deployed to ensure that the procession of 17 May 2012 took place peacefully.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The second to fourteenth applicants submitted written statements describing the exact circumstances surrounding the incident of 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: At around 1 p.m. on 17 May 2012, members of the LGBT community, staff members of Identoba and other LGBT activists, including the second to fourteenth applicants, gathered at the Tbilisi Concert Hall area, totalling approximately thirty people.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Shortly before the beginning of the demonstration on 17 May 2012, members of the Orthodox Parents' Union arrived in the Tbilisi Concert Hall area.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Shortly before the beginning of the demonstration on 17 May 2012, members of the Saint King Vakhtang Gorgasali's Brotherhood arrived in the Tbilisi Concert Hall area.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Journalists were present at the Tbilisi Concert Hall area shortly before the demonstration on 17 May 2012, recording interviews with the LGBT marchers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Approximately 200 metres from the starting point of the march on 17 May 2012, members of the Orthodox Parents' Union and the Saint King Vakhtang Gorgasali's Brotherhood confronted the LGBT marchers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: When the LGBT marchers reached Rustaveli Avenue on 17 May 2012, they were met by a hundred or more counter-demonstrators who were particularly aggressive and verbally offensive.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The counter-demonstrators blocked the LGBT marchers' way on Rustaveli Avenue by making a human chain and encircling the marchers, making it impossible for them to pass.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The LGBT marchers were subjected to threats of physical assault and to insults by the counter-demonstrators on Rustaveli Avenue on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The LGBT marchers, feeling threatened on 17 May 2012, immediately telephoned the police to alert them to the danger and request the immediate dispatch of additional police forces.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: While waiting for additional police support on 17 May 2012, the LGBT marchers noticed a few police officers present at the scene on Rustaveli Avenue.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: When the LGBT marchers approached the police officers present at the scene on 17 May 2012 and asked for help, the officers replied that they were not part of the police patrol and it was not their duty to intervene.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: After approximately twenty to thirty minutes of escalating aggression on 17 May 2012, counter-demonstrators grabbed banners from the hands of several LGBT activists and tore them apart.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Counter-demonstrators resorted to physical attack by pushing and punching the LGBT marchers in the front row on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: As a result of the counter-demonstrators' assault on 17 May 2012, the sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili), who was in the front line of the march, was knocked down, beaten and kicked.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Shortly after the assault on the sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili), several police patrol cars arrived at the scene on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Some law-enforcement officers intervened by stopping the beating of the sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Police officers separated the opposing parties on 17 May 2012 by standing between the LGBT marchers and the counter-demonstrators.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: At the time police officers separated the parties on 17 May 2012, the aggressive and agitated counter-demonstrators were still making particularly vitriolic threats against the marchers.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The third applicant (Mr L. Berianidze), who was standing on the pavement with other LGBT marchers on 17 May 2012, asked the police to take more active measures to protect the demonstration.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The police responded to the third applicant (Mr L. Berianidze) by forcing him into a patrol car on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The police drove the third applicant (Mr L. Berianidze) to the Old Tbilisi Police Department of the Ministry of the Interior on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The third applicant (Mr L. Berianidze) was detained at the Old Tbilisi Police Department of the Ministry of the Interior for approximately twenty minutes on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The third applicant (Mr L. Berianidze) was given no official explanation for his arrest at the time of his detention on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: As subsequently explained by the Government, the police had sought to distance the third applicant (Mr L. Berianidze) from the scene on 17 May 2012 in order to protect him from the angry counter-demonstrators.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili), the seventh applicant (Ms G. Dzerkorashvili) and the tenth applicant (Ms M. Kalandadze), all employees of Identoba, were arrested by the police on 17 May 2012 when they moved from the pavement to the road.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The sixth, seventh and tenth applicants (Mr G. Demetrashvili, Ms G. Dzerkorashvili and Ms M. Kalandadze) were forced into police patrol cars and driven around the city for approximately twenty minutes before being returned to Rustaveli Avenue on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: As subsequently explained by the Government, the aim of the short-term retention of the sixth, seventh and tenth applicants on 17 May 2012 was to prevent them from committing an administrative offence of impeding road traffic.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: As subsequently explained by the Government, the aim of the short-term retention of the sixth, seventh and tenth applicants on 17 May 2012 was also to protect them from the counter-demonstrators' assault.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Later on 17 May 2012, the third applicant (Mr L. Berianidze) sought medical help for his injuries.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Later on 17 May 2012, the sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) sought medical help for his injuries.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The third applicant (Mr L. Berianidze) was found to have a bruised left knee, grazes on his left palm and fingers, a haemorrhagic forearm and a haematoma on the right eyebrow.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) was found to have a closed head trauma, cerebral contusions, and bruises on the left side of his chest.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 19 May 2012, the fourteenth applicant (Ms M. Tsutskiridze) visited a doctor.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The fourteenth applicant (Ms M. Tsutskiridze) was diagnosed with a contusion of the left wrist.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The clashes between the LGBT marchers and counter-demonstrators on 17 May 2012 were recorded by journalists present at the scene.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The footage of the clashes between the LGBT marchers and counter-demonstrators on 17 May 2012 was broadcast in the evening of 17 May 2012 by a number of national television channels.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The faces of the applicants who had been attacked and the assailing counter-demonstrators were clearly recognisable in the broadcast footage of the clashes of 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 18 May 2012, members of the board of the first applicant organisation filed several complaints with the Ministry of the Interior concerning the violent acts committed during the march of 17 May 2012 by representatives of the Orthodox Parents' Union and the Saint King Vakhtang Gorgasali's Brotherhood.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 18 May 2012, members of the board of the first applicant organisation filed several complaints with the Chief Public Prosecutor's Office concerning the violent acts committed during the march of 17 May 2012 by representatives of the Orthodox Parents' Union and the Saint King Vakhtang Gorgasali's Brotherhood.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The complaints filed on 18 May 2012 were mostly based on the account of the circumstances as described in the thirteen individual applicants' written statements.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 19 May 2012, a criminal investigation was launched into the infliction of light bodily harm on the fourteenth applicant (Ms M. Tsutskiridze) by unidentified persons.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: When questioned as a witness on 19 May 2012, the fourteenth applicant (Ms M. Tsutskiridze) stated that unidentified men had grabbed her poster and hit her with the handle of the poster.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 23 May 2012, the eighth applicant (Ms E. Glakhashvili) was questioned about the fourteenth applicant's (Ms M. Tsutskiridze's) injury to her hand.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 21 June 2012, a forensic medical examination was commissioned by the investigation into the fourteenth applicant's (Ms M. Tsutskiridze's) injuries.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The forensic medical examination commissioned on 21 June 2012 found that the bruising and excoriation the fourteenth applicant (Ms M. Tsutskiridze) had sustained on her wrist represented light bodily injuries.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The fourteenth applicant (Ms M. Tsutskiridze) was not granted victim status within the framework of the criminal investigation opened on 19 May 2012 at that time.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 26 June 2012, the first applicant received a letter from the deputy director of the police patrol department of the Ministry of the Interior in response to the board members' complaints of 18 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The letter of 26 June 2012 from the deputy director of the police patrol department of the Ministry of the Interior stated that there were no signs of illegality in the actions of the police during the demonstration of 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The letter of 26 June 2012 from the deputy director of the police patrol department of the Ministry of the Interior stated that there was no need to launch an investigation against the police for abuse of power.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: Two counter-demonstrators had been arrested for transgression under Article 166 of the Code of Administrative Offences (minor breach of public order) in connection with the events of 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The two counter-demonstrators arrested for minor breach of public order under Article 166 of the Code of Administrative Offences were each fined 100 Georgian laris (approximately 45 euros) in connection with the events of 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 3 July 2012, the first applicant and the second to fourteenth applicants filed additional criminal complaints with the Chief Public Prosecutor and the Minister of the Interior.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 5 July 2012, the first applicant and the second to fourteenth applicants filed additional criminal complaints with the Chief Public Prosecutor and the Minister of the Interior.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In their criminal complaints of 3 and 5 July 2012, the applicants specifically requested that a criminal investigation be launched on account of the verbal and physical attacks perpetrated against them by the counter-demonstrators with clear discriminatory intent.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In their criminal complaints of 3 and 5 July 2012, the applicants specifically requested that a criminal investigation be launched on account of the acts and/or omissions of the police officers who had failed to protect them from the assaults on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In their criminal complaints of 3 and 5 July 2012, the applicants emphasised that criminal inquiries should be conducted with due regard to Article 53 of the Criminal Code of Georgia, which provided that the existence of homophobic intent was an aggravating circumstance in the commission of a criminal offence.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The criminal complaints of the third, sixth, seventh and tenth applicants focussed on the attacks against them by the counter-demonstrators and the lack of police protection during the incident of 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The third, sixth, seventh and tenth applicants did not request an inquiry into the alleged restriction of their liberty by the police during the incident of 17 May 2012 under Article 147 of the Criminal Code of Georgia.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: By a letter of 17 July 2012, the Ministry of the Interior replied to the first applicant and the second to fourteenth applicants that during the incident of 17 May 2012 the police had called upon both the LGBT marchers and the counter-demonstrators to exercise their right to demonstrate in a peaceful manner.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The Ministry of the Interior's letter of 17 July 2012 reiterated the information concerning the imposition of administrative sanctions on two of the counter-demonstrators, namely their arrest and fine of 100 Georgian laris each under Article 166 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 24 October 2012, a criminal investigation was opened into the alleged beating of the sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) by unidentified persons on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 24 October 2012, the sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) was interviewed as a witness in the criminal investigation into his alleged beating.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) stated when interviewed on 24 October 2012 that he had been encircled and insulted by five or six counter-demonstrators on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) stated when interviewed on 24 October 2012 that the attackers had started kicking and hitting him on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) stated when interviewed on 24 October 2012 that the ill-treatment on 17 May 2012 lasted for a few minutes until a police officer finally intervened and removed him from the scene.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: On 6 November 2012, a forensic medical expert issued an opinion confirming that the sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) had sustained a contusion and closed head trauma.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) was not granted victim status at the time of the criminal investigation opened on 24 October 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In September 2014, the two counter-demonstrators who had previously been fined for administrative misconduct in connection with the events of 17 May 2012 were examined as witnesses in relation to the beating of the sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili).
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In September 2014, the sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) was questioned again about the incident of 17 May 2012 and stated that he could no longer remember certain circumstances due to the significant lapse of time.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: In September 2014, the sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) confirmed that he would still be able to recognise the faces of those individuals who had assaulted him on 17 May 2012.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the latest information available in the case file, the criminal investigation opened on 19 May 2012 into the light bodily injuries sustained by the fourteenth applicant (Ms M. Tsutskiridze) is still pending.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: According to the latest information available in the case file, the criminal investigation opened on 24 October 2012 into the light bodily injuries sustained by the sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) is still pending.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The sixth applicant (Mr G. Demetrashvili) has never been granted victim status in the criminal investigation into his injuries.
section_path: I. THE CIRCUMSTANCES OF THE CASE

text: The fourteenth applicant (Ms M. Tsutskiridze) has never been granted victim status in the criminal investigation into her injuries.

text: On 27 March 2012, an amendment to Article 53 of the Criminal Code of Georgia was adopted pursuant to which discrimination on the grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity was recognised as a bias motive and an aggravating circumstance in the commission of a criminal offence.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW. INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS AND OTHER MATERIALS
A. Criminal Code, as in force at the material time

text: Article 53 § 3(1) of the Criminal Code of Georgia provides that the commission of any offence listed in the Criminal Code on the grounds of any type of discrimination, including that linked to race, skin colour, language, sex, sexual orientation and gender identity, age, religion, political and other views, disabilities, citizenship, national, ethnic or social background, origin, economic status or societal position or place of residence, shall be an aggravating circumstance.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW. INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS AND OTHER MATERIALS
A. Criminal Code, as in force at the material time

text: Article 117 of the Criminal Code of Georgia proscribed the offence of intentional infliction of severe physical injuries.

text: Article 118 of the Criminal Code of Georgia proscribed the offence of intentional infliction of less serious physical injuries.

section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW. INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS AND OTHER MATERIALS

section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW. INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS AND OTHER MATERIALS

text: Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 was adopted by the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe on 31 March 2010 on measures to combat discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW. INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS AND OTHER MATERIALS
B. Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe to member States on measures to combat discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity

text: Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 provides that member states should ensure effective, prompt and impartial investigations into alleged cases of crimes and other incidents where the sexual orientation or gender identity of the victim is reasonably suspected to have constituted a motive for the perpetrator.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW. INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS AND OTHER MATERIALS
B. Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe to member States on measures to combat discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity

text: Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 provides that member states should ensure that particular attention is paid to the investigation of crimes and incidents allegedly committed by law enforcement officials or by other persons acting in an official capacity, and that those responsible are effectively brought to justice and, where appropriate, punished in order to avoid impunity.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW. INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS AND OTHER MATERIALS
B. Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe to member States on measures to combat discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity

text: Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 provides that member states should ensure that when determining sanctions, a bias motive related to sexual orientation or gender identity may be taken into account as an aggravating circumstance.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW. INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS AND OTHER MATERIALS
B. Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe to member States on measures to combat discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity

text: Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 provides that member states should take appropriate measures to ensure that the right to freedom of expression can be effectively enjoyed without discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity, in accordance with Article 10 of the Convention.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW. INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS AND OTHER MATERIALS
B. Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe to member States on measures to combat discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity

text: Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 provides that member states should take appropriate measures at national, regional and local levels to ensure that the right to freedom of peaceful assembly, as enshrined in Article 11 of the Convention, can be effectively enjoyed without discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW. INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS AND OTHER MATERIALS
B. Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 of the Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe to member States on measures to combat discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity

text: Recommendation CM/Rec(2010)5 provides that member states should ensure that law enforcement authorities take appropriate measures to protect participants in peaceful demonstrations in favour of the human rights of lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender persons from any attempts to unlawfully disrupt or inhibit the effective enjoyment of their right to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly.
section_path: II. RELEVANT DOMESTIC LAW. INTERNATIONAL DOCUMENTS AND OTHER MATERIALS
